works.abstract_text: Extending Zhu's Pell-prime result (2011), we refute the conjecture in OEIS A320043, COMMENTS, revision 43 (September 8, 2022; posed December 16, 2018), by a(708158976)=144767444036350576^2. For every prime p, its preceding row has sum p^2(p^2-1)/12; for p>=5, this sum is a square exactly when p^2-12y^2=1 for an integer y. An elementary descent recovers the known Pell sequence and proves that this is the smallest additional square index whose successor is prime. We also reprove the known power-of-two index restriction, give a factor excluding the proposed next candidate in A277434, and prove the triangle's product identity and an all-row divisor formula.

works.abstract_text: Extending the spectral bounds of Sun, Luo and Ye [Mathematics of Operations Research 45, 233–271 (2020)], we refute the arbitrary-rank interpretation of the pointer-product conjecture of Abbott, Silva, Wechs, Brunner and Branciard [Quantum 3, 194 (2019), Section 4, p. 5, after equation (26); arXiv:1805.09364v3]. Three orthogonal projections on C^3 give the normalized weak-limit pointer product -1/6 < -1/8. For n measurements in unrestricted finite dimension, the exact minimum is -c_n, where c_1=0 and c_(n+1)=(1+c_n)^2/[8(1-c_n)]. Codimension-one projections attain every finite-length minimum, and c_n increases to 1/3. Thus pointer products have infimum -1/3, separated by 2/3 from the limiting ordered weak value -1. The same bounds hold as envelopes at every finite coupling strength for independent centered Gaussian pointers.

works.abstract_text: We answer Problem 30 in Section 9 (p. 27) of Alfuraidan, Khan and Sauras-Altuzarra, Metric dimension and maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of graph Laplacians, arXiv:2610.26875v1, and extend the metric-dimension classification of Knor, Sedlar and Škrekovski (2022) to a classification of both maximum spectral multiplicities for Theta(3,3,r), for every r >= 2. For every integer k >= 1, the theta graph with edge lengths 3, 3, 6k+4 is connected and twin-free, has metric dimension and maximum Laplacian eigenvalue multiplicity two, and has simple signless spectrum. Its only repeated Laplacian eigenvalues are 1 and 3, each double. Distinct orders give pairwise nonisomorphic examples. For r >= 3, repeated eigenvalues are classified modulo six; r = 2 has a separate quadratic repeated factor. Attaching an equal pendant path at every vertex of two known base graphs also gives twin-free infinite families in both separation directions.

works.abstract_text: We answer Section 4, item 3 of Alikhani and Griswold's On the Integer Domination Root Conjecture by constructing connected graphs with domination root −4 and unbounded order. Joining r copies of their 33-vertex graph through vertices adjacent to leaves gives a connected graph on 33r vertices whose domination polynomial is the rth power of the original polynomial. The root −4 has multiplicity exactly r, and the copies can be joined along a path with maximum degree seven. A mixed construction gives examples of every order at least 35, with maximum degree seven and cycle rank four. We give a complete set-bijection proof, an exact finite calculation for the base graph, and the scope of the corresponding Lean declarations.

works.abstract_text: We prove Anthony Browne's conjecture in OEIS A164660, final FORMULA (29 May 2016): for every positive integer n, the reduced numerator of the integral from 0 to 1 of T_(n+1)(x) equals the stated floor product and (-1)^(n/rad(n)). Both sides are +1 exactly when 4 divides n. The same calculation proves the preceding rational-integral conjecture and gives its denominator sequence A164661. More generally, replacing the exponent n in the product by any integer r >= 2, and translating its interval by any integer, leaves the product unchanged. We give the exact root count for every r >= 1 and correct two coefficient-table discrepancies in the linked sources.

works.abstract_text: Bajnok–Beatty Conjecture 4.1 in arXiv:2406.04045v1, Section 4, p. 10, asks which groups Z/2Z × Z/(2k)Z have a two-element signed spanning set of radius s. The note proves its four-case classification for all positive k,s. A near-square relation-lattice argument gives the necessary congruences, and explicit constructions give sufficiency. Coefficient-residue counts also prove Conjecture 1.6 (Section 1, p. 3): for s≥3, the maximum noncyclic order is 2s² if 2s+1 is prime, and 2s²+2s−(p²−1)/2 otherwise, where p is the smallest prime divisor of 2s+1. The attaining constructions are those of Bajnok and Beatty. The bounds in Theorems 1.8, 3.2 and 3.3 hold without regularity. For Conjecture 1.10 the note proves cyclicity for two generators and corrects the printed multiplier domain by an explicit perfect set in Z/13Z.

works.abstract_text: For Bernáth's consecutive-ratio conjecture in OEIS A400645, revision 21, COMMENTS, we prove the stronger bounded-error asymptotic a_n=c lambda^n+O(1) with c>0, where lambda is the largest real root of x^8-x^6-x^4-x^2+1, namely 1.3122819079.... The squared terms satisfy a linear recurrence with a controlled rounding error. A finite seed bounds its entire normalized error tail and ensures a positive leading coefficient; a three-coordinate contraction then gives an exponential asymptotic. The same error analysis proves the ratio assertions for A063827 and A400644, and extends them to nondecreasing initial data. We also prove the increasing-sequence conjecture in A289916 and recover its limiting ratio, identified in A289917.

works.abstract_text: We refute the mixed-state inverse sumset estimate expected in Remark 45, equation (58), of Bu, Gu and Jaffe, Quantum Ruzsa Divergence to Quantify Magic (arXiv:2401.14385v3). A computationally diagonal equal mixture of two basis states in dimension seven has quantum-doubling constant sqrt(2) and relative entropy log(7/2) from its mean state, while the proposed bound is at most (1/2)log(7). The contradiction uses exact inequalities and persists for every tensor power. For the same family, we verify that the weaker estimate (59) has a positive denominator and holds strictly, and give the equality case of the companion entropy-growth statement for computationally diagonal states.

works.abstract_text: We refute Conjecture 4.2 in Section 4, p. 13, of Dovgoshey and Rovenska, arXiv:2610.11596v1, extend their (2026) central-edge bounds, and derive companion corollaries from Petrov's (2022) homogeneous-tree characterization and Dovgoshey et al.'s (2026) perfect-binary-tree theorem. A four-point ultrametric has six central edges against four in a metric. For every n >= 4, the three-central minima are 2 ceil(n/2) over metrics and 2n - 4 + ceil(n/2) over ultrametrics. Conjecture 4.1 is corrected to orders 1 and even; Problem 4.3 has minimum order 1 for k=1, k for even k, and k+1 for odd k >= 3. Earlier counterexamples to Conjecture 4.1 by Love (2023) and Bargetz et al. (2024) are credited. For every feasible pair with n >= 3, the metric edge minimum is (k-1) ceil(n/2). The tree corollaries give the isometry groups and sphere counts of minimum-order ultrametrics, with explicit coverage of the related questions.

works.abstract_text: We prove the conjecture in §2.9 of Lester, Haddadin and Gripaios, Lorentz and permutation invariants of particles III (arXiv:2008.05206v6), that their three-variable sets S and S-hat are minimal for their respective four-particle event classes. Any two continuous, Lorentz- and pair-permutation-invariant, parity-odd real variables vanish together on a chiral collision event. The proof constructs a sphere consisting entirely of chiral events, on which parity acts antipodally up to the allowed symmetries, and applies the two-dimensional Borsuk-Ulam theorem. The same obstruction holds for strictly timelike, momentum-completable collisions with any number of additional interchangeable momenta, and for fully interchangeable collections of at least four momenta.

works.abstract_text: The surjectivity question in the final paragraph of Section 5, p. 9, of Delgado, Süer and Yeşil's A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups (arXiv:2611.14268v1) has a negative answer: pseudo-Frobenius row deletion always leaves 1 as a gap. The symmetric numerical set {0,1} union {n >= 4} is therefore not in the image. In fact, at least half of all symmetric numerical sets with any prescribed odd Frobenius number at least 3 are excluded. Every symmetric numerical semigroup, in contrast, is fixed by the map. We identify the entire fiber over the target with sole gap 1 and obtain at most 2^(floor((F+1)/2)-1) distinct images of sources with Frobenius number F.

works.abstract_text: We refute the trace-distance case of axiom (T4) of Denis, Lacaille, Martin and Serrano-Ensástiga (arXiv:2605.29436v1, Section III.A.2, Eq. (7)–(8)), where “a proof is left open.” An explicit SU(2)-covariant channel decreases the order-seven anticoherence of a mixed spin-four state by exactly 95/90552, disproving the universal validity suggested by their reported numerical evidence. The channel is a normalized sum of quadrupole Kraus operations; its covariance and trace preservation follow from Cartesian tensor identities. Both reduced states are diagonal, so the strict inequality reduces to rational arithmetic. We reconstruct an existing spin-four witness and give a self-contained exact counterexample within the full mixed-state domain of the proposed axiom.

works.abstract_text: Extending Han–Pedon's lower-shift results (2026), we prove their Conjecture C (arXiv:2610.36132v1, p. 6): for every n ≥ 1 and ℓ ≥ n+3, every residue subsequence of the shifted q-metallic Hankel determinants is a rational polynomial, from its first term, with period 2n(n+1) for even n and 4n(n+1) for odd n. Each polynomial is integer-valued on all integers. A complementary-minor formula reduces the determinant to a matrix of fixed size with polynomial dependence on the number of continued-fraction periods. We give a degree bound, rational generating functions, constant-coefficient recurrences and periodicity from the first term modulo every positive integer at every shift. Exact complementary-minor identities and the degree bound prove the affine laws extending Ovsienko–Pedon's golden shift-4 pattern (2023; published 2025).

works.abstract_text: The all-length earliest-swapping conjecture in Section IV D 1, Eq. (41), of Kamin, Shchukin, Schmidt and van Loock (2023) states that repeatedly merging an adjacent pair with smallest maximum ready time minimizes total dephasing. We give a self-contained potential proof for arbitrary nonnegative real ready times and every tie choice. The optimum is the largest ready time plus the sum of adjacent maxima minus the sum of ready times. An exact nonnegative slack formula characterizes all optimal histories. The pathwise inequality also answers the exponential-dephasing question in Section IV D 5, for the same fixed-readiness swapping model: earliest swapping simultaneously minimizes expected dephasing and maximizes every expected exponential attenuation factor.

works.abstract_text: We answer Kang–Jäger's Question 1.10 (arXiv:2609.01140v1) negatively, including its strictly ergodic and Toeplitz versions. We construct one aperiodic regular Toeplitz subshift over the binary alphabet such that, for every permutative block code of every length ell >= 2, the entire inverse image is conjugate over the base to the product with the identity on 2^(ell-1) points. Each lift therefore has exactly 2^(ell-1) clopen strictly ergodic components. The construction uses recognizable equal-length words with factorial repetition counts: these annihilate every finite permutation action, while the proportion of columns on which the two words differ is exactly 3^(-n).

works.abstract_text: Koljančić–Oblak's Problem 1.8, Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra 42 (2026), p. 759, has an affirmative answer: the minimum number of arcs in an n-vertex digraph requiring the nonsymmetric strong spectral property is 2n−1 for every n≥1. By their identification with Arav et al.'s Problem 6.2, this also gives the minimum 2n−1 of nonzero entries in a zero–nonzero pattern requiring the similarity-transversality property (STP). We give a self-contained exposition of the centralizer–incidence proof formalized in Lean. More generally, every real matrix with this property and with c weak support components has at least 2n−c nonzero entries. For connected supports, even allowing one such matrix forces 2n−1 arcs. Together with the endpoint-looped double path of Koljančić–Oblak, this also answers both questions in their Problem 2.9 (p. 764). The endpoint construction is prior work.

works.abstract_text: Question 5.11 of Koljančić and Oblak (arXiv:2604.21552v1, Section 5; journal p. 776) has an affirmative answer: every even double path with a nonempty loop set allows the non-symmetric Strong Spectral Property. We construct a symmetric one-loop witness using coprime branch continuants and prove injectivity of its characteristic-polynomial differential. Openness then supplies every prescribed nonempty loop set. The same argument gives a complete existence criterion in odd order: at least one loop must lie at an odd-numbered vertex. The witnesses can be chosen symmetric with positive integer nonzero entries. Carptopus (19 August 2026) previously proved the full existence criterion and its single-loop spectral characterization. We give an explicit integer construction, an arithmetic criterion for unit edge weights, and the three-way classification for the central-loop and interior-loop families.

works.abstract_text: Extending Moothathu's progression-exclusion construction (2010), we answer the open Question 5.6 of Meddaugh and Stephens (arXiv:2509.04312v1, Section 5, p. 12; 2025) affirmatively by constructing a mixing, surjective binary forward subshift with neighborhood 2-shadowing and a nonempty clopen set containing no nonempty periodic set. The subshift forbids an all-one arithmetic progression of length p^2+3 and difference p, for each positive integer p. Two separated deletion masks from a quadratic-irrational rotation trace every sufficiently accurate pseudo-orbit. The same construction is not of quasi-finite type, giving a further affirmative example for Question 5.3 (Section 5, p. 11), and has no ordinary shadowing. The same conclusions hold for every progression-length function ell(p)>=3 with ell(p)/p tending to infinity, without a monotonicity assumption. Each of the two tracing points can trace at a syndetic set of times, despite failure of quasi-finite type.

works.abstract_text: Extending Maestro's exact qutrit separation (2026) by the unitary-moment obstruction of Dykema and Juschenko (2009), we refute Conjecture 1 of Narasimhachar and Gour (arXiv:1409.7740v3, Supplementary Sec. S2 F, p. S11) even in the closure of finite ground-space thermal transitions. Two diagonal Kraus operators send the uniform pure state of a four-level system with energies 0, 1, 3, 7 to a rank-two state with the same populations. Any energy-conserving realization with an ancilla initially maximally mixed on its full ground eigenspace would express the output correlation matrix as normalized traces of four unitaries. Two linear relations make that representation impossible, with a dimension-independent gap. The trace-norm error of any such thermal output exceeds 10^-8. A three-vector projection obstruction also refutes Conjecture 2 in versions 1 and 2 of the posing source. The four-level obstruction extends to every system with at least four occupied distinct energy levels. Together with the known qutrit closure theorem, this makes four the minimum dimension for closure separation under distinct-level and distinct-gap assumptions.

Every planar or toroidal graph is non-CN-hyperenergetic. For every finite nonabelian group, its noncentral commuting graph satisfies E_CN ≤ n(n-z-2) < 2(n-1)(n-2), where n counts noncentral elements and z counts central elements; the same bound holds for every finite noncommutative ring, without an identity assumption. The group argument combines the published estimate E_CN ≤ 4m with a proper-centralizer count. A neighborhood-clique decomposition proves the surface statement. For a union of cliques, equality with the complete-graph benchmark occurs exactly for one clique or two isolated vertices.

works.abstract_text: We prove Paul Curtz's six-residue denominator conjecture in OEIS A189733, revision 12, COMMENTS (May 23, 2011), now in revision 36, FORMULA, with its convention that zero has denominator one. Following Gao's earlier generating-function proof, we derive exact values of the first row of the defining rational array. These values also prove the six-periodic numerator assertion, the denominator recurrence, and Barker's empirical generating function in the same entry. The same formulas settle Barker's recurrence and generating-function conjectures in A267068 and give the numerator identities in A278718. We also prove the full-array reflection and binomial-transform identity. The corresponding second-kind array yields A194767's denominator formulas and reciprocal sum, and corrects an index in its fourth-diagonal numerator identity. For the unsigned-seed array in A189731 and A242926, the same argument gives a Lucas-number formula and refutes the asserted prime-only integer ranks at the composite 705. An integer triangular transformation determines antidiagonal denominator lcms for arbitrary rational seeds.

works.abstract_text: We prove Conjectures 9.63 and 9.64 in Section 9.8.3 of Okada's arXiv:2003.02112v2. Conjecture 9.66, whose width is at least three, is proved on degree-shift slices e=0,1,G-1,G and at e=G/2 when G is even, where G is the direct-minus-reversed degree gap. works.abstract_text: We resolve the nonlinear classical k=6 factor-perfection question of Pozsgay and Wanless, §5 immediately after equation (5.13), and their qubit decomposition conjecture in §8 for both constructions studied there (k=6,8). For arbitrary finite-alphabet gates, a perfect six-leg composite forces perfect factors. Six specified permutation flattenings characterize this property. A norm–determinant argument gives the quantum analogue for unitary gates, extending the prior forward construction of §3.2, Theorems 1–2. For arbitrary complex factors, the same six unitary exterior flattenings guarantee perfect replacement tensors at the same bond dimension. This excludes every six-qubit AME state from the three-vertex triangle with bond dimension two. The eight-qubit case follows from known AME nonexistence (Rains, DOI 10.1109/18.796376; Scott, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevA.69.052330).

works.abstract_text: The Shannon conjecture following Eq. (69) in Section V.C of Tarabunga et al., arXiv:2411.05766v1, is false. An explicit three-qubit state has stabilizer-basis entropy log 4, whereas the proposed absolute-amplitude lower bound is log 16 - (9/8) log 3 > log 4. The same construction refutes the bound for nonnegative amplitudes, and continuity gives strictly positive examples. It extends to every N >= 3 and to a range of Renyi indices containing one. The collision entropy of the comparison distribution remains a valid Shannon lower bound for arbitrary affine supports. For amplitudes of constant modulus on each affine coset, the original bound holds at every Renyi index; this includes the source's Figure 1 product states.

works.abstract_text: We resolve User3's question (question 515549, revision 1, September 25, 2026): for every nonsingular real square matrix of positive size, the orthogonal minimum of rho(|PQ||Q^T P^{-1}|) is attained and equals one. Thus the proposed strict uniform lower bound cannot hold for any such matrix. We give a self-contained exposition of the triangularization proof in the pinned formal source, then characterize every minimizer by independent row and column permutations to triangular form. For fixed P, the set of minimizers is finite and has an explicit description using row-permuted QR factorizations. The same minimum holds over the special orthogonal group. Finally, the companion absolute-row-sum balancing question follows from the Yamabe-Yujobo theorem.

works.abstract_text: We answer the realizability question of Vélez Caicedo and Cadavid (§5, p. 17, second paragraph of arXiv:2611.14316v1) by reflecting semigroup generators about a prescribed maximum jump: every numerical semigroup T is realizable, and a positive integer M is an admissible maximum exactly when M belongs to T and every minimal generator h satisfies h<2M and 2M-h belongs to T. The construction gives the unique inclusion-minimal jump set at each admissible maximum and realizes every sufficiently large maximum. Using the source's spectral formulas, we also recover the semigroup from two global dimensions and M-2 restricted dimensions when M>=2. For prime maxima, eventual dimensions at proper-divisor moduli alone need not distinguish semigroups.

works.abstract_text: We refute Conjectures 3.26 and 5.3 of Wang's Semigroup rings and algebraically independent sequences with respect to idempotents in commutative semigroups (arXiv:2509.18724v1, pp. 23 and 27). The commutative periodic monoid of finite subsets of the natural numbers, paired with levels zero, one and two under union and capped addition, has algebraic Davenport constant one over every nonzero commutative unitary ring. Its nongroup relative Davenport constants are unbounded. The finite submonoids with supports contained in {1,...,m}, m>=1, have the same algebraic constant, whereas the expression conjectured to equal it grows without bound as m increases.

works.abstract_text: For OEIS A344611, FORMULA (revision 27), we prove A344611(n) <= A160786(n) for every n >= 0 and give an alternative derivation of Manyama's (2026) convolution, complementing Andrews–El Bachraoui's (2026) strict-partition formulas. An injection sends a partition with nonnegative reverse-alternating sum to an odd-length partition of the next weight. We characterize equality, give an explicit lower bound for the deficit, and deduce monotonicity of the corresponding unrestricted count. The same parity analysis proves a shifted companion comparison, determines all plateaus of the negative-sum count, and corrects neighboring indexing and distinct-part descriptions. A bivariate series settles the linked ordered-composition interpretations, with their precise shifts.

works.abstract_text: The question in Xu et al., Section 4.2, page 12 of arXiv:2211.05563v1, asks whether the optimized witness bound equals the convex-roof geometric measure of genuine multipartite entanglement for noisy GHZ states. A strict separation holds for every party count n >= 3 and local dimension d >= 3 at an explicit noise probability. For three qutrits at noise p=3/8, the optimized witness bound is exactly 1/9, whereas the convex roof is at least 13/108. A biseparable overlap inequality and a positive-definite matrix give a two-observable lower bound. A written corollary extends the three-qutrit strict gap throughout 27/74 < p < 9/22.
